policy.goal: Finish the native C rewrite of ../quake-typescript as one engine with full Q1/QW/Q2/Q3, expansion, rerelease, and mod interoperability, then perform a deep performance and enhancement pass.
rules: Sequence: write the complete baseline code, review code quality throughout, finish all baseline implementation, then evaluate gameplay/frame time and perform deep performance gains and polish.

Do not make early playability, FPS, profiling, pixel polish, or campaign playthroughs prerequisites for baseline coding. Use proportionate compile, static, ownership, parser, and logic checks while coding.
Port Anthology functionality and intent. ../qsrc is reference material and ../qfiles contains external assets; do not replace the target with three original engines.
Implement built-in gameplay as compiled C with direct shared services. Remove TypeScript-only machinery. Scope external program compatibility to actual requirements.
Share common code, asset data, GPU resources and buffers. Preserve necessary private state and source behavior. Ordinary C floats are allowed where behavior is retained.
No functionality cuts, lower quality, removed renderer, fewer entities, reduced AI or lost campaign/mod behavior to gain speed.
Review actual code as it is implemented. A dependency permits integration/acceptance only after its prerequisites are complete; source implementation may overlap when published interfaces suffice.
Use vibecheck-jev to claim/report work and its verified status. Keep the full dependency graph and acceptance criteria current.
Coordinator owns shared Git staging and local commits. Workers use exclusive paths and never change ../quake-typescript, ../qsrc, or ../qfiles.
Baseline completion and final release are distinct. Do not claim whole-project completion from scaffolding, parser tools, compilation, or partial subsystems.
authorizations: Implement the entire project autonomously, make sensible C improvements during construction, and continue until the full project is complete.
Create and commit code, tests, documentation, build files and dependency metadata locally.
Use read-only source/assets and proportionate local verification.
Delegate independent bounded implementation tasks with exclusive file ownership.
stop_reasons: Explicit user request to stop or pause.
A concrete external prerequisite that cannot be obtained or worked around within authorization; continue independent work and report it.

tasks.label: Register the implementation graph
tasks.goal: Publish the complete dependency graph and current user rules to vibecheck-jev; keep a reviewable local copy.
criteria: Ledger and local graph cover all 23 donor functional targets; baseline completion precedes gameplay evaluation and deep enhancement.

tasks.label: C build and core foundation
tasks.goal: Implement the C17 build, error and ownership types, checked binary access, file I/O, memory utilities, and native executable entry.
criteria: GCC and Clang compile the native target; focused boundary and ownership checks pass; no Bun runtime dependency.

tasks.label: Archive readers
tasks.goal: Implement shared PAK and ZIP/PK3/PK4 readers with ordered entries, normalized paths, stored/deflated extraction, and corruption checks.
criteria: Real archives and focused malformed-input cases are read correctly; stored data can be shared without repeated copying.

tasks.label: Mounts and shared resource ownership
tasks.goal: Implement loose/archive mounts, precedence, content identity, caching, lifetimes, and writable overlays.
criteria: One mount/resource service resolves identities and shares immutable data across game families without merging distinct content.

tasks.label: Map formats
tasks.goal: Implement Q1/Q2/Q3 map formats and required variants, record readers, entity text, visibility, and extensions.
criteria: Donor-supported BSP variants have checked C readers; source records and extensions retain required semantics.

tasks.label: Models and images
tasks.goal: Implement model/image formats, palettes, sprites, animation data, replacements, and attachments.
criteria: All required donor formats have C readers and common retained resources; no supported format silently drops records.

tasks.label: World identity and collision
tasks.goal: Implement generational actors, source slots, authoritative bodies, link state, geometry, collision, and spatial queries.
criteria: One shared world retains source link timing, allocation/reuse, query shapes, and tie ordering in focused checks.

tasks.label: Session scheduling and lifetime
tasks.goal: Implement source clocks, callback order, mutation authority, session lifecycle, transition coordination, and component lifetime.
criteria: Scheduling and nested mutation use explicit owners; session creation, teardown, actor reuse, and rollback checks pass.

tasks.label: Movement and player commands
tasks.goal: Implement all selected Q1/QW/Q2/Q3 and rerelease movement policies, player command processing, and prediction kernels.
criteria: Native C kernels support independent per-player movement with required source cadence, bounds, and numeric decisions.

tasks.label: Combat inventory and composition
tasks.goal: Implement shared damage, inventory, pickups, capacities, effects, component operations, and attack provenance.
criteria: Each mutation has one authority; ordered transforms, observers, replacements, and private state retain required behavior.

tasks.label: Q1 built-in gameplay
tasks.goal: Implement Anthology Q1/QW base, expansions, rerelease, monsters, weapons, items, and source gameplay in native C.
criteria: Full Q1 family roster and behavior are implemented through shared services, including mission-pack and rerelease distinctions.

tasks.label: Q2 built-in gameplay
tasks.goal: Implement Anthology Q2 classic, expansions, rerelease, monsters, weapons, items, and source gameplay in native C.
criteria: Full Q2 family roster and behavior use compiled gameplay; stock and rerelease selections do not invoke CPU emulation.

tasks.label: Q3 built-in gameplay
tasks.goal: Implement Anthology Q3 and Team Arena gameplay, weapons, items, characters, and source rules in native C.
criteria: Q3 and Team Arena behavior is implemented through shared services and remains independently selectable.

tasks.label: Campaigns and authored interactions
tasks.goal: Implement entity target graphs, mission gates, keys, sigils, bosses, hubs, revisits, authored mechanisms, and travel.
criteria: Campaign code preserves authored obligations when actors or equipment are replaced; transitions have one owner.

tasks.label: Modes objectives and equipment
tasks.goal: Implement independent match modes, teams, scoring, cross-map objective adaptation, grapples, and offhand equipment.
criteria: Required modes and equipment variants are connected to shared gameplay without coupling map, arsenal, or movement selection.

tasks.label: Product catalog and configuration
tasks.goal: Implement installed products, editions, launch recipes, independent selections, preset defaults, and mod catalog.
criteria: Configuration resolves the full feature union with atomic changes and explicit source identities.

tasks.label: Scene materials and resources
tasks.goal: Implement shared scene, visibility, materials, models, lights, effects, and frame/resource ownership.
criteria: Required family-specific presentation behavior uses one scene/resource system with CPU/GL backend contracts.

tasks.label: CPU renderer
tasks.goal: Implement the complete software rasterizer and source rendering semantics.
criteria: Clipping, textures, palettes, interpolation, depth, stencil, fog, and blending have implementation and focused checks.

tasks.label: GL renderer and display
tasks.goal: Implement native GL rendering, retained buffers, SDL window/context lifecycle, capture, and backend restart.
criteria: Required render features are wired to real native APIs with correct resource lifetime; no frame-time tuning gate.

tasks.label: Audio and media
tasks.goal: Implement decoding, music, source voice policy, mixing, per-seat audio, cinematics, synchronization, and devices.
criteria: All required audio/media formats and policies have shared C implementations and lifecycle checks.

tasks.label: Input and local seats
tasks.goal: Implement keyboard/mouse/controllers, gyro, haptics, text input, device lifetime, and four local seats.
criteria: Per-seat routing and state remain independent; focus loss, unplug, and reassignment release owned input correctly.

tasks.label: Console settings localization
tasks.goal: Implement commands, cvars, profiles, bindings, settings, text/font resources, localization, and accessibility.
criteria: Source command semantics and persistent configuration are exposed through shared services.

tasks.label: QC compatibility
tasks.goal: Implement external QuakeC programs, host imports, private instances, composition, and checkpoints.
criteria: Original QC roles and required extensions connect to shared services; built-in gameplay remains native C.

tasks.label: QVM compatibility
tasks.goal: Implement external QVM game, cgame, and UI roles, syscall profiles, private instances, composition, and checkpoints.
criteria: Required QVM semantics and source profiles work through shared engine boundaries without another world.

tasks.label: Native module compatibility
tasks.goal: Implement required original native module ABIs using host-native execution where suitable and scoped fallbacks where required.
criteria: Required binary callbacks, private instances, composition, and saved state are implemented; no default port of TS CPU machinery.

tasks.label: Independent mod integration
tasks.goal: Integrate multiple cross-game mod instances, controls, ownership, dependency order, presentation, commands, and objectives.
criteria: Actual module adapters compose through common operations; enable/disable, private state, and rollback are implemented.

tasks.label: Bots and navigation
tasks.goal: Implement one Q3-derived player-bot core, useful rerelease features, shared navigation generation, and source monster paths.
criteria: Bots use ordinary engine actions and selected gameplay; foreign maps have usable navigation implementation.

tasks.label: Network transport and codecs
tasks.goal: Implement original protocol dialects, transport, reliability, per-seat connections, IPX/KEX requirements, and Anthology packets.
criteria: Explicit codecs preserve required dialects; one connection authority serves native and mixed sessions.

tasks.label: Network session and prediction
tasks.goal: Integrate authoritative remote play, commands, snapshots, prediction, travel, reconnect, and full mixed-session identities.
criteria: Native and Anthology session state is wired to gameplay with correct command ownership and replay behavior.

tasks.label: Downloads browser and administration
tasks.goal: Implement downloads, remounting, server discovery, hosting, authenticated administration, and rotation.
criteria: Required acquisition/discovery/admin flows have production consumers and cleanup behavior.

tasks.label: Saves recovery and demos
tasks.goal: Implement shared/original saves, migration, level-entry autosaves, recovery, demos, MVD/GTV, journals, and VCR.
criteria: Persistence retains all owners; legacy exports reject unrepresentable state; save/demo formats have explicit codecs.

tasks.label: Progression and player services
tasks.goal: Implement progress, achievements, records, Q3 unlocks, lobbies, and ranking-provider interface.
criteria: Required local/player services have consumers; only the previously approved unavailable ranking backend remains an extension point.

tasks.label: Menus HUD and guest presentation
tasks.goal: Implement native menus, per-seat HUD, source/guest UIs, content selection, independent mod controls, and all settings.
criteria: Every required menu/HUD/service workflow is connected to real engine implementations.

tasks.label: Tools cameras capture and LLM
tasks.goal: Implement camera/tools/diagnostics/capture and existing LLM provider, cancellation, and command integration.
criteria: Required public tools and assistance have native application consumers; no invented external service.

tasks.label: Application integration and packaging
tasks.goal: Wire the complete baseline executable, dedicated mode, startup/shutdown, delivery layout, and asset discovery.
criteria: All required subsystem implementations are linked and reachable; ordinary build/static/correctness checks pass; no placeholders or disconnected feature implementations.

tasks.label: Complete baseline release code
tasks.goal: Finish the entire baseline implementation before gameplay evaluation and the deep performance pass.
criteria: All required code exists, is integrated, and builds with reviewed ownership and focused correctness checks; baseline completion is not a claim of polished gameplay or final qualification.

tasks.label: Full gameplay and interoperability evaluation
tasks.goal: Evaluate completed baseline campaigns, native/mixed modes, mods, saves, networking, rendering, audio, and devices; fix defects.
criteria: Document actual coverage and resolve required behavior failures without removing functionality.

tasks.label: Deep performance pass
tasks.goal: Profile the complete engine and make deep CPU, GPU, memory, allocation, threading, and latency improvements.
criteria: Matched real workloads demonstrate improvements while preserving required behavior, content, effects, and simulation work.

tasks.label: Enhancement and polish
tasks.goal: Complete presentation, interaction, responsiveness, and further worthwhile enhancements on the completed engine.
criteria: Enhancements preserve the entire feature union and have proportionate validation.

tasks.label: Final full-project qualification
tasks.goal: Qualify the completed and enhanced engine for delivery with all declared required functionality.
criteria: Required campaigns, configurations, mod and peer workflows, packaging, and performance results are accounted for; limitations are explicit and no required work is silently dropped.
